text:
You want a Next.js blog setup with an EditorJS-based post creation workflow that can take a short user prompt, call OpenAI from a server-side API route, and return structured content the editor can render and expand section by section.

I can build that workflow cleanly in your existing blog template and keep it aligned with the stack you outlined: Next.js, EditorJS, fetch-based client requests, and an OpenAI-backed API route that returns EditorJS-friendly JSON. I’ll set it up so the editor first asks for a 2–3 sentence topic description, sends that to your project’s API route, and then renders the generated outline and title back in EditorJS for review. I can also add the custom button/plugin behavior for outline headings so each section can trigger body generation in the same experience.

I’ve built a similar content-processing workflow in Python for Vantor Call Centers: a call centre speech analytics pipeline that transcribed calls, separated agent and customer using speaker diarization, and wrote a QA summary for every call. That system processed 2,300 hours of audio, brought word error rate to 11.8%, and increased QA coverage from 3% to 100% of calls. While that project was in a different domain, the core patterns are the same: structured AI output, reliable API handling, and turning raw input into reviewable content.

For your blog generator, I’ll focus on:
- setting up the blog from the existing template while skipping the pieces you don’t want
- replacing Netlify deployment with Vercel
- adding an online EditorJS interface
- creating a server-side OpenAI integration for outline generation
- structuring the returned content in the JSON format EditorJS expects
- implementing the custom heading controls for section-by-section expansion

I’m comfortable working across Python, machine learning, NLP, and OpenAI API integrations, and I’d bring the same careful approach to the Next.js and EditorJS implementation here. If you’d like, I can keep the build practical and modular so the generator is easy to extend later with richer drafting behavior.
